cases.story: An authorized application reuses a live, correctly scoped cached policy value.
The cache is empty; a current admitted source supplies and caches the policy.
The request arrives exactly at TTL expiry. The receiver refreshes from the current source.
A still-live cache entry exists after the current access grant is revoked.
Only another tenant's same-named object is cached. It must not be disclosed to tenant-a.
The origin changes to version2/value2000 while version1 remains within TTL.
Admitted source and cache agree on a false value. Freshness and matching metadata do not establish truth.
A stale entry cannot be refreshed because the origin is unavailable; the owner explicitly admits recorded deferment.
Origin generation changes after cache qualification but before use. A final local check defers without disclosing the old value.

evidence_ceiling: Actual local SQLite cache/source data and traces; own specified policy, no Redis/HTTP/Azure cache, distributed atomicity or measured performance win.
